2
Which expression gives an SI base quantity?
A
charge per unit time
B
force per unit area
C
mass per unit volume
D
work done per unit distance

hints: Recall the seven SI base quantities: mass, length, time, current, temperature, amount of substance and luminous intensity.
Rewrite each phrase as a division, such as charge divided by time and force divided by area, and name the quantity formed.
Check which of current, pressure, density and force is in the SI base list rather than a combination of base quantities.
walkthrough: List what each expression means: charge per unit time is $Q/t$, force per unit area is $F/A$, mass per unit volume is $m/V$, work done per unit distance is $W/d$.
Name the resulting quantity in each case: $Q/t$ is current $I$, $F/A$ is pressure $p$, $m/V$ is density $\rho$, and $W/d$ is force $F$.
Recall that electric current is one of the seven SI base quantities, while pressure, density and force are all derived quantities made from combinations of mass, length and time.
Current has the SI base unit ampere, $\text{A}$, whereas the others have derived units such as $\text{Pa}$, $\text{kg m}^{-3}$ and $\text{N}$.
Therefore charge per unit time gives an SI base quantity. This is option A.

A.explanation: Charge per unit time is $I = Q/t$, which is electric current with SI base unit ampere $\text{A}$.

B.explanation: Force per unit area is $p = F/A$, which is pressure with derived unit pascal $\text{Pa}$.

C.explanation: Mass per unit volume is $\rho = m/V$, which is density with derived unit $\text{kg m}^{-3}$.

D.explanation: Work done per unit distance is $F = W/d$, which is force with derived unit newton $\text{N}$.
